Perhaps, while watching him flame-broil the Toronto Raptors, Miami Heat and Sacramento Kings this week — to the tune of 127 points in 106 minutes on 37-for-70 shooting with 20 3-pointers in a three-game span — you found yourself thinking, "Man, Luka Dončić is on an all-time heater to start the season."
 Well, if it seems that way, it's because he very, very much is:
 "You need three guys to guard him," Lakers big man Sandro Mamukelashvili said, according to ESPN . "I have a feeling that every time Luka plays, it's like 35-plus [points]."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pretty close, Mamu. It's actually six times in eight games this season. (The last six, if you're keeping score.)
 Much of the postgame commentary about Dončić's performance in the Los Angeles Lakers' 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday focused on his defensive work : on the 15 defensive rebounds he pulled down, on the five steals he snagged and six deflections he piled up, on the charges he took to draw offensive fouls and get the Lakers another possession. That certainly matters; Dončić is no stranger to catching hell for lacking defensive effort on the sport's grandest stage , and these Lakers will need him to put his best foot forward on that end if they hope to get back to that stage themselves.
 "We've been relying on our offense a lot," Lakers center Walker Kessler told reporters after a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers last week. "And we have a very, very good offense and a lot of great scorers. But that's not gonna be the only thing that gets us to win a championship here."
 It won't. It'll be the main thing, though. Because what the Lakers did, after ending the somewhat awkward stuck-between-stations stint that stretched from Dončić's arrival at the 2025 trade deadline and the team bidding farewell to LeBron James this summer, was build A Luka Dončić Team. And if there's one thing A Luka Dončić Team is going to do, it's score a truckload of points — with the lion's share of them coming off the fingertips of No. 77, who might be playing the best basketball of his career at this very moment.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I don't know," Dončić told reporters after Wednesday's win over the Kings. "I've had some good stretches in my career. Obviously, these could be one of the highest ones."
 Sunday's monstrous performance against the Raptors made Dončić just the second player since the NBA began tracking steals in 1973 to score 45 points, collect 15 rebounds, dish 5 assists and grab 5 steals in a single game — joining, as luck would have it, Anthony Davis , the man whom the Lakers traded to Dallas to secure Dončić's services nearly two years ago. It was his 24th career 45-point game , tying George Gervin for 10th on the all-time list, and his 11th career 45-point, 10-rebound, 5-assist outing — more than anybody but Laker legends Wilt Chamberlain and Elgin Baylor.
 Monday's just-as-massive attack on the visiting Heat represented Dončić's 29th 40-point, 10-assist game — third-most ever, behind only Oscar Robertson and James Harden. And he did it on the second night of a back-to-back, in a performance that made no less an authority on dominance than a two-time NBA Most Valuable Player stand up and take notice. From ESPN's Dave McMenamin :
 "Obviously, he's one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best," [Giannis] Antetokounmpo said after L.A. improved to 6-2 with the win over the struggling Heat (2-5).
 A reporter interrupted Antetokounmpo's answer, hoping for additional context for the two-time MVP's claim.
 "Right now?"
 "Not right now," Antetokounmpo replied. "Not right now. Of all time. I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he's got to be up there."
 In a related story: After hanging another 40-ball on the Kings on Wednesday, Dončić has totaled 308 points through his first eight games of the season. He's just the fourth player in NBA history to score 300 or more points in the first eight games of a campaign, and the first since Michael Jordan did it in 1988. (He's also the first player in NBA history to top 300 points, 50 rebounds and 50 assists through eight games, according to Justin Kubatko of Statitudes .)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dončić has a long way to go to climb to the top of that "best scorers to play this game" list in sheer scoring volume. He's tallied 15,329 points through eight-plus NBA seasons, good for 163rd on the all-time ABA/NBA scoring list , and 27th among active players . On a per-game basis, though? When the only two names above you on the all-time list are MJ and Wilt , you must be doing something right. And right now, Luka's doing an awful lot right.
 Eight times, Dončić has suited up for the Lakers this season; five times, he's topped 40 points. He is now averaging 1.08 points per minute , a historical rate of offensive onslaught; the only other player who's even cracked 1.0 was Wilt, 65 years ago .
 This isn't normal. Luka just makes it seem that way.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal," Lakers head coach JJ Redick told reporters after Sunday's win. "We live on a spaceship and we're going at the speed of light at all times when he's on the court."
 Dončić has opened the season looking like the best damn pilot in the galaxy, leading the NBA in scoring at 38.5 points per game, 8.4 points more than second-place Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That 8.4-point gap between first and second place is roughly the same as the gap between SGA and his cousin, Atlanta Hawks swingman Nickeil Alexander-Walker, whose 21.7 points per game rank 28th in the NBA.
 "I don't even know how to explain the shots he makes," Kessler said Wednesday . "I mean, it's like, when it goes up, regardless of how he got to the shot, it's just like, 'Well, so that's probably going in' […] Right now he's playing the best basketball in the league."
 Dončić leads the NBA in field goals made per game, in 3-pointers made and attempted per game, and in free throws made and attempted per game. He's converting on all those looks at or near career-best rates , shooting 83% at the rim, 59% from floater range, 54% on midrange looks overall, 89% from the free-throw line, and 43.1% from long distance. He's also fifth in the NBA in assists, dishing 8.0 dimes per contest, making him one of two players in the top 10 in both categories, alongside Jayson Tatum of the Boston Celtics. Combine the points that Dončić is generating by setting up his big men at the rim and shooters on the perimeter with the ones that he's scoring himself, and he's creating 57.5 points of offense for the Lakers per game — most in the NBA, according to Databallr .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Including plays where he shoots or passes to a teammate who shoots, Dončić's pick-and-rolls are producing 1.102 points per play, the 10th-highest mark among players who've run at least 50 pick-and-rolls, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking. His isolations are generating 1.211 points per possession — sixth-best among players who've finished at least 25 one-on-one trips. When he orchestrates from the post, the Lakers have scored 1.222 points per trip — eighth-most among players to log at least 10 such plays.
 Add it all up, and the Los Angeles offense has been an absolute buzzsaw with Luka at the controls. The Lakers have scored a scorching 131.1 points per 100 non-garbage-time possessions in Dončić's minutes ; as a point of comparison, the league-leading Trail Blazers offense averages 122.6 . They're shooting the cover off the ball from everywhere with him on the floor : 79% at the rim, 58% from midrange and 42% from 3-point land.
 They've been elite in the half-court , with Dončić poking and prodding and bending coverages until they snap. They've been even better in transition , where Dončić's combination of excellent defensive rebounding for a wing and perpetual eyes-up scanning for hit-ahead opportunities allow L.A. to get out and run into easy buckets:
 "When he has it going, it's like, pick your poison, cause he can just make any shot," Redick said. "And then you start putting two on the ball, and everybody else is the beneficiary of that. He's a terrific offensive engine."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That engine is running red-hot to start the season, pacing the Lakers to a 7-2 record behind the NBA's No. 2 offense , with Dončić playing like an MVP frontrunner — and getting the help he needs from the Lakers' other core pieces.
 Second banana Austin Reaves is averaging 23.3 points and 5.0 assists per game on 53/43/88 shooting, and playing some of the best defense of his career … well, on Luka, at least:
 New center Kessler is holding up his end of the bargain, shooting 71.4% from the field, averaging 14.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game, and holding opponents to a microscopic 42.6% at the rim when he's the closest defender; that's the fourth-best mark of any interior deterrent to face at least 30 up-close shots, according to Second Spectrum tracking .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement All told, the Lakers have blitzed opponents by 100 points in 163 minutes with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler on the court together — the second-best point differential of any three-man unit in the league thus far — and their core lineups have largely been lights out, with a number of role players (Mamukelashvili, Jake LaRavia, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, et al.) providing the right kind of production and filling in the gaps around that high-priced, high-wattage core.
 The spaceship could hit some turbulence, though. The Lakers have played one of the league's easier schedules thus far; four of their seven wins have come against the Clippers, Jazz and Kings, who have a combined record of 3-21. They're also outperforming their expected field goal percentage to a higher degree than any other team in the league, according to multiple shot-quality metrics .
 If that red-hot collective shooting normalizes — and if the ball-security issues that have L.A. ranking 27th in team turnover percentage , with Dončić and Reaves sitting second and third in the league in total cough-ups — then the Lakers could be in for some regression … especially if, y'know, Luka doesn't continue to average 38 points per game on Prime Steph shooting and Prime Harden usage for a full season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Of note: Luka's never gotten to the basket less. His 16.8 drives per game are his lowest average since his rookie season , and a career-low 8% of his shot attempts have come at the rim, according to Cleaning the Glass . He's balanced that out by taking more than half of his attempts from 3-point land for the first time in his career, which is a pretty good idea when you're making them; what happens, though, if those stepbacks aren't cashing in at a 43% clip?
 If and when that comes, some of the Lakers' other shortcomings — the hole at power forward, the lack of another viable ball-handler to help Reaves buoy the offense when Dončić rests, the worrisome lack of rebounding and interior heft when Kessler's off the floor, etc. — could become more glaring. For now, though, the Lakers are off to what's been by and large a glass-half-full start: a top-of-the-league offense with a just-below-average defense , outscoring opponents by 9.3 points-per-100 (a 62-win pace ), with Dončić looking like the best player on the floor damn near every time he sets foot on it, somehow making the obscene look routine.
 "It's a really good offense that we're playing right now," Redick said Monday . "A lot of that, of course, is Doncic and what he's able to do and bend the defense. His shotmaking creates a lot of problems, and then he can make every pass."
 It doesn't seem possible that a spaceship like these Lakers can keep going at the speed of light without eventually slowing down. That's the thing about superstars like Dončić, though: When they've got it going, the limits of physics and history and even our imaginations can just seem to fade away.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "All of the great, great players that have ever played have also been in the 1% competitor [level]," Lakers assistant coach Greg St. Jean recently told Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times . "They've always been the guy that is able to inspire the players around him and be able to do things that don't even seem like they're possible. And he does that nightly."
